thread.title: Garmin: Future Outlook And Fair Value Estimate - Garmin Ltd. (NASDAQ:GRMN)

author: Dilantha De Silva
title: Garmin: Future Outlook And Fair Value Estimate - Garmin Ltd. (NASDAQ:GRMN)
text:
Investment thesis Garmin (NASDAQ: GRMN ) was once thriving in the portable navigation devices industry, but soon became the victim of the rise of smartphones and in-built navigation systems in vehicles. Since then, Garmin has successfully diversified its product portfolio and has managed to overcome the negative effects of the declining automotive segment. The underlying macroeconomic condition is favorable at the moment, but there are signs of increasing competition, which might lead to price wars in the future. Garmin is currently trading with a dividend yield of over 3%, but there is limited upside potential.
Company overview and business strategy Garmin manufactures GPS devices and develops GPS software. The company is operating in 5 distinct segments.
Automotive Aviation Marine Outdoor Fitness wearables Over the last decade, Garmin has shifted its core business focus from automotive products to other products as the automotive segment started losing its steam as a result of the rise of free mapping and navigation products.
Over the last couple of years, Garmin has focused more on growing inorganically as well and has completed several acquisitions successfully.
(Source: Crunchbase )
The company has openly acknowledged the deteriorating outlook of the automotive segment, and has been continuously working toward building a diversified product portfolio to tackle this issue. Improving contribution to company revenues from the marine and aviation segments remain one of the core business strategies at the moment. On the other hand, Garmin is committed to distributing wealth to its shareholders via dividends and this has been outlined on many occasions by the company's management.
The fitness wearables segment has also been exposed to fierce competition from well-known brand names of late and remaining a key player in this market is another core business strategy of the company.
Overall, the future profitability of the company will mostly depend on how Garmin would be able to offset the expected decline in the automotive segment by growing revenues from the other segments.
Industry analysis and future outlook Garmin operates in various niche segments and hence, the future outlook of each one of these segments should be analyzed individually. In this analysis, I will discuss the macroeconomic outlook of every segment along with company prospects in the same segment.
Automotive segment
The automotive segment looks the least attractive of the lot, and this segment is expected to continue its decline over the next few years. Since peaking in 2011, worldwide unit shipments of Portable Navigation Devices (PND) have declined drastically, primarily driven by the rise of in-built navigation systems and the use of smartphones.
Worldwide unit shipments of portable car navigation devices (2010-2015)
(Source: Statista )
Macroeconomic headwinds have resulted in a massive erosion of profits for Garmin from this segment, but this has not stopped Garmin from pursuing other avenues for growth in the automotive segment, which are discussed below.
Geely Auto Group has selected Garmin to provide its camera technology and driving recorder systems, starting from 2020. Even though Geely is not a highly recognized name in the Western world, it is surely one of the fastest growing automakers in China.
Geely is reportedly the third largest automaker in China, and has surpassed Nissan ( OTCPK:NSANY ) and Honda (NYSE: HMC ) in vehicle sales and the growing popularity of Geely vehicles provide a robust growth opportunity for Garmin as well.
Most importantly, Garmin will be partnering with Geely to provide camera and recording systems for most models manufactured by Geely, as per the CEO.
“Yes. So, the camera solutions that we're providing to Geely are across most of their models in China, there is regulation around having camera systems in vehicles, so it is equipment that is required in the vehicle. Timing will be the model year 2020 when the first model start rolling out, so we'll start ramping up in later 2019” – Clifton A. Pemble
In addition to this deal, Garmin has been selected by BMW AG ( OTCPK:BMWYY ) as a supplier of OEM infotainment products, and with this deal, Garmin will work with BMW AG in China to improve the in-vehicle offering of navigation facilities. As per company filings, Garmin will be working with BMW AG from 2020.
The automotive segment is clearly experiencing massive declines in unit sales as this market was centered on portable navigation devices in the past. However, Garmin has made meaningful progress by securing deals with automakers, and these deals will contribute to the company's top line from 2020. Therefore, even though the industry headwinds have continued to hurt Garmin for the best part of the last decade, the company is expected to recover from its lows in the automotive industry.
Aviation and marine segments
The use of GPS in aviation is increasing rapidly. Improving the safety of passengers has been one of the most focused areas in the aviation industry, and this is expected to remain the same in the future. In line with this renewed interest in improving safety measures, the demand for GPS products has increased, as technologically advanced GPS devices are significantly improving the decision-making process.
The marine segment is also set to grow based on the increasing demand for GPS products from the recreational boating category.
Even though both aviation and marine segments represent a small portion of the global GPS market, both these segments are expected to pick up significantly through 2025.
(Source: Grand View Research )
Garmin is actively positioning the company to benefit from this expected growth in the industry. Garmin is building a new aviation manufacturing facility in Olathe, which is expected to double the current manufacturing capacity. On the other hand, the company has already been recognized as the manufacturer of the year by the National Marine Electronics Association, which establishes the company’s commitment toward introducing innovative products in this segment.
Outdoor and fitness wearables
The outdoor segment includes wearables such as smartwatches, and this segment is expected to grow exponentially in the next decade. However, the level of competition is also expected to increase in line with the massive popularity of smartwatches and other wearables.
(Source: Statista )
Overall, this segment presents a robust growth opportunity for Garmin, but fierce competition might result in price wars in which case Garmin will not become the favorable player to come out on top.
In line with this expected growth in the wearables segment, Garmin is continuing to provide innovative solutions. Garmin has successfully integrated Spotify with the Fenix 5 Plus series, which enables users of this smartwatch to download Spotify playlists to the watch.
Fenix 5 Plus
(Source: Garmin)
Garmin is committed to expanding their outdoor wearables offering and the company recently announced Instinct, which is another GPS smartwatch. To enhance the user experience, Garmin is working on improving the Connect IQ store , which is the flagship app store for Garmin devices.
However, as noted earlier, competition will continue to increase and this poses a major threat for Garmin’s survival as an industry leader. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) and Fitbit (NYSE: FIT ) are disrupting the global smartwatch market, and Garmin is already finding it difficult to keep up pace with the growth in popularity of alternative devices.
Almost all the smartwatch vendors are seeing a massive surge in smartwatch shipments except Garmin, which underlines a core problem for the future growth of Garmin.
(Source: Counterpoint Research )
Smart wristbands market is also expected to blossom for many years to come, driven by the increased demand for fitness trackers.
Forecast unit shipments of smart wristbands (2016–2022e)
(Source: Statista )
The overall industry outlook remains positive, but there are headwinds especially in the automotive segment. Garmin is focused on navigating through difficult times in the automotive segment by securing deals with automakers and at the same time, the company has already penetrated into other industries such as aviation and marine successfully. The future outlook is promising, but increasing competition will probably have a negative effect on company earnings, if this competition leads to a price war.
Evaluation of financial performance Garmin has topped analyst estimates in each of the last 4 reporting periods on the back of strong revenue growth over comparison periods. Increased diversification in its product portfolio has helped Garmin achieve stellar financial performance despite the significant decline in revenue of the automotive segment.
(Source: Nasdaq )
A quick look at Gamin’s historical revenue figures is helpful in determining how the company is continuing to recover from the massive decline in the auto segment. From 2008 to 2013, revenues continued to decline before picking up once again on the back of innovative product launches.
(Source: Author prepared based on data from company filings)
From being a secondary contributor to Garmin’s top line in 2009, the outdoor/fitness segment has grown to become the largest contributor to company revenues at present. Aviation and marine segments have also picked up over the last decade.
Segmental revenue breakdown (2009–2017)
(Source: Statista )
Another important development with regard to Garmin’s profitability over the last few years is the expansion in profit margins. Operating efficiency has improved significantly over the last 5 years, supporting the expansion in profit margins over the same period.
(Source: Author prepared based on data from company filings)
(Source: Morningstar )
Despite having had to overcome a tough little period, Garmin still operates with zero leverage which places the company in an attractive position to move forward into the future. On the other hand, Garmin continues to generate sufficient free cash flow to cover for its capital expenditures and dividends. Despite a pullback in free cash flows as the auto segment revenues declined, Garmin has recovered quite well over the last 3 years.
(Source: Author prepared based on data from company filings)
Garmin is in a growth phase powered by improving industry dynamics and company fundamentals. Financial performance of the company has been robust over the last 3 years but investors need to factor in a possible increase in competition across all products offered by Garmin.
Garmin as a dividend play Though it seems unlikely at first, Garmin should be considered a strong candidate for a place in a dividend focused portfolio. Shares currently offer a yield of above 3% and company fundamentals support further hikes in dividends.
Dividend history
(Source: Street Insider )
Not only is the dividend yield attractive, it is safe from a fundamental perspective as well, which is discussed below.
(Source: Author prepared based on data from company filings)
Garmin has consistently been able to cover its dividend payments with free cash flows, which is a good starting point in assessing the sustainability of dividend payments. On the other hand, Garmin has maintained an acceptable payout ratio , which has historically allowed the company to allocate capital efficiently between shareholder distributions and capital investments, and will continue to do so in my opinion.
As noted earlier, Garmin operates with zero debt, which provides shareholders with an additional measure of safety regarding the dividends.
Despite the expected headwinds, I believe Garmin is positioned well to continue paying the current level of dividends and dividend-focused investors have an opportunity to invest in Garmin when the yield is still above 3%.
Valuation So far, this analysis has established a few points about Garmin from an investor’s perspective.
The industry outlook for Garmin is positive, but Garmin will be met with fierce competition for its products from well-known names in the tech industry. Garmin is a safe dividend play, even after accounting for a slowdown in growth. The company has attractive fundamentals and sound financial health. However, calculating an intrinsic value remains the most important step in the investment decision-making process as the current market price should be evaluated against such an intrinsic value estimate to arrive at an investment decision.
In this analysis, I have used a discounted cash flow method to value Garmin with a discount rate of 9.5%. The terminal value calculation was completed using exit multiples.
Revenue growth forecast
The wearables segment, which is the largest contributor to company revenues and profits, is expected to grow at a double-digit rate for the next 5 years, and there will be mid to high single-digit growth in the aviation and marine segments. However, a further decline in the automotive segment is expected, but the negative effect will be partly offset by additional revenue streams that are expected to contribute to the top line of the company from 2020.

EBITDA margin
The historical EBITDA margin over the last 5 years has remained close to 25% on average, and I believe this trend will continue in the next 5 years as well. Despite improving prospects, I believe Garmin will be faced with fierce competition, which might lead to a price war between companies operating in the industry. Therefore, I do not believe that EBITDA margins will improve significantly over the next 5 years, but at the same time, a significant deterioration looks unlikely as well.
Capital expenditures
Capital expenditures have risen significantly over the last 3 years, which is a trend that I expect to continue. Among other things, the company is focused on improving its manufacturing facilities related to the aviation segment, which will require further capital investments. On the other hand, Garmin is planning to relocate its distribution center. As per remarks from the company's management, a renovation of office premises is also on the cards during the next 5 years.
All of this will contribute to higher capital expenditures in the forecast period, along with investments toward improving technological aspects of the product portfolio. Capital expenditures might decline significantly beyond the forecast period as the aviation and marine industries mature, and growth opportunities diminish.
(Source - Author prepared based on data from company filings)
I have forecast capital expenditures to represent 5% of company revenue in 2019, and then decline to a more sustainable rate of around 3.5% at the end of the forecast period.
Exit multiples
I have used an EBITDA multiple to determine the terminal value of Garmin. The 5-year average EV/EBITDA multiple stands at 12, but I have used a multiple of 9.5 in calculating the terminal value in order to reflect the expected slowdown of company growth and the deterioration of investor sentiment that comes with it.
With these assumptions, I arrived at a fair value estimate of $59.59 for Garmin shares, which indicates a downside of 10% from the current market price of $66.57.
Conclusion The prevailing macroeconomic condition should help Garmin achieve greater profitability in the future, but the current market price is more than reflective of this expected growth. From the perspective of dividends, the company is still an attractive play, but there is limited upside potential from the current market price. The company is currently earning economic profits, but its ability to continue to do so will come into question as competition increases dramatically over the next half a decade. I believe shares are fairly valued and investors should wait for a better entry point.
